topic: waste sorting (bunrisugeori): pay-per-bag trash, weighed food waste, sorted recycling
title: In Korea, Taking Out the Trash Has Rules

slides.headline: In Korea, your trash **has a rulebook.**
slides.note: Bags you buy, bins you sort, food you weigh.

slides.headline: It's called **bunrisugeori**
slides.body: 분리수거, sorting waste by type. Paper, plastic, cans, glass, vinyl and styrofoam each get their own bin.

slides.headline: Trash goes in **bags you buy**
slides.body: Since 1995, general trash must go in official bags sold at convenience stores. The bag price is the fee.

slides.headline: Food scraps **get weighed**
slides.body: Many apartments have a smart bin. Tap a card, drop the scraps, and pay by the kilogram.

slides.headline: Bones? **Not food waste.**
slides.body: In Seoul, chicken bones, egg shells and onion skins go in general trash. Each city sets its own list.

slides.headline: Clear bottles, **labels off**
slides.body: Clear plastic bottles go in their own bin. Empty, label peeled, crushed flat.

slides.headline: Why **people follow it**
slides.body: Get it wrong and the bag can be left behind. Dumping can mean a fine of up to ₩1 million.

slides.headline: Food waste **recycled**
slides.body: About 2% in 1995. 96% by 2019, turned into animal feed, compost and biogas.

slides.headline: Elsewhere one bin. **Here, six.**
slides.body: In many cities the truck takes it all. In Korea, sorting is your job, and the bag price makes it pay.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: Neat row of colored recycling bins at a Seoul apartment complex at dusk, softly blurred behind the text.

caption:
In Korea, taking out the trash comes with rules: bags you buy, bins you sort, food scraps you weigh.

Recycling here starts in your kitchen, not at a plant.

How many bins do you sort into where you live?
reply: One more: a big item like a sofa or a mattress can't just go out on the curb. You report it to your district, pay a small fee, and stick the receipt on it before it's picked up. What's the strangest trash rule where you live?
fact_check: 3장: 쓰레기 수수료 종량제 1995-01-01 전국 시행(1994-04 서울 시범). 규격봉투 편의점·마트 판매, 지자체별 디자인.
4장: RFID 음식물 종량기 — 카드 태그, 무게별 수수료(서울시 권장 방식). 'many apartments'로 표기.
5장: 서울시 2022 통일 기준 — 동물·생선뼈, 조개껍데기, 달걀껍데기, 양파껍질 = 일반쓰레기. 춘천 등은 다름(전국 통일 기준 없음).
6장: 투명 페트병 별도 배출 — 공동주택 2020-12-25, 단독주택 2021-12-25. 내용물 비우고 라벨 제거, 위반 시 과태료 30만원 이하.
7장: 규격봉투 미사용·무단투기 과태료 최대 100만원(폐기물관리법). 미수거 스티커는 관행.
9장: 일반화 — 혼합 수거 도시가 많다는 비교. 특정국 단정 안 함.
댓글: 대형폐기물 — 구청 신고·수수료 납부·배출 스티커(필증) 부착.
